module.title: Unit 8: Advanced Spoken Nuance: Sarcasm, Understatement & Irony
module.objective: Mampu mendeteksi dan menggunakan litotes (understatement), ironi bersahabat, dan modulasi intonasi penutur asli.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Reading Between the Lines
subModules.grammarFocus: Understatement, verbal irony, and rhetorical questions
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Words for irony, sarcasm, humour, and spoken intonation

content.summary: Read a short story about a school presentation and notice how speakers use understatement and friendly irony. You will practise looking beyond the literal meaning of a sentence, using context and intonation clues to understand the speaker's real message.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Notice understatement with phrases such as “a bit” and “not exactly,” positive words used ironically, and rhetorical questions that express frustration.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Learn words for understatement, sarcasm, deadpan humour, irony, and pitch.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Read first for the situation and the speakers' relationships. Then look for contrast between what someone says and what has happened, as well as clues in their reactions and intonation.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a short B2 story about a school presentation.
Locate details that show whether a comment is friendly, critical, or genuinely positive.
Recognise understatement, verbal irony, and sarcastic rhetorical questions in context.
Use word choice, situation, and pitch clues to infer a speaker's intended meaning.

contextWarmup.prompt: Your friend arrives ten minutes late in heavy rain and says, “Lovely weather for a walk.” What is the most likely meaning?
options: Your friend is making a playful comment about the unpleasant weather.
Your friend thinks the weather is perfect for walking.
Your friend is asking you to go for a walk later.
contextWarmup.explanation: The comment contrasts with the heavy rain, so the situation suggests friendly verbal irony rather than a serious opinion.

rules: Understatement makes a situation sound less serious or extreme than it is. Phrases such as “a bit” and “not exactly” can soften criticism or create humour.
Verbal irony often uses positive words to describe an unpleasant or disappointing situation. The surrounding events and the speaker's tone help reveal the intended meaning.
Sarcasm can sound sharper than friendly irony and may express irritation or criticism. A rhetorical question is not always a real request for information.
Pitch, stress, pauses, and facial expression can change how a comment sounds. A flat delivery may make a joke sound deadpan, while a falling or exaggerated pitch can signal irony.

commonTrap.explanation: Taking an ironic comment literally can lead you to misunderstand the speaker. Check whether the words fit the situation and consider how other people respond.
commonTrap.wrong: The room is flooding, and someone says, “Well, this is going perfectly.” The reader decides that the speaker is pleased.
commonTrap.correct: Notice the contrast between the words and the flooded room. The speaker is likely using irony to show that the situation is going badly.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Understatement and Verbal Irony
grammarFormulas.description: Assemble sentence blocks to practise softened comments, ironic statements, and rhetorical questions:

complements.text: a bit differently from what we planned

items.exampleSentence: Calling the flooded classroom a little damp was an understatement.

items.meaning: sarkasme; ejekan yang disampaikan dengan ironi
items.exampleSentence: His sarcasm made it clear that he was annoyed about the delay.

items.meaning: ekspresi datar; tanpa ekspresi wajah saat melawak
items.exampleSentence: She gave a deadpan reply, and the class laughed.
His tongue-in-cheek claim that he was the school's best singer made his friends smile.
It was ironic that the technology club's presentation had no working screen.
Her pitch fell at the end of the sentence, making the joke sound dry.

items.meaning: intonasi; perubahan nada suara saat berbicara
items.exampleSentence: His rising intonation made the short remark sound like a question.
“Who could have seen that coming?” was a rhetorical question.

items.meaning: penekanan pada kata atau suku kata
items.exampleSentence: Extra stress on the word “brilliant” showed that she did not mean it literally.
By saying the plan was a bit ambitious, he implied that it was unlikely to work.

content.passageTitle: A Slight Problem with the Presentation
paragraphs: On Friday, Maya and Leo presented their science project to the class. Just before they began, the screen went black and their slides disappeared. “Well, this is a brilliant start,” Maya said, stressing “brilliant” and letting her pitch fall. Leo smiled, so she knew he understood the irony. Their teacher offered to restart the computer, but the class was already waiting.

After a minute, the slides returned, though the first one was upside down. “The technology is having a bit of a difficult day,” Leo said, using understatement to keep everyone relaxed. Maya added, “What could possibly go wrong now?” Her question was rhetorical, and her deadpan expression made the class laugh. They carried on without more trouble. Afterwards, Maya said the presentation had gone “not exactly as planned,” which was a gentle way to describe a stressful start.

timestamps.text: On Friday, Maya and Leo presented their science project to the class.
Just before they began, the screen went black and their slides disappeared.
“Well, this is a brilliant start,” Maya said, stressing “brilliant” and letting her pitch fall.
Leo smiled, so she knew he understood the irony.
Their teacher offered to restart the computer, but the class was already waiting.
After a minute, the slides returned, though the first one was upside down.
“The technology is having a bit of a difficult day,” Leo said, using understatement to keep everyone relaxed.
Maya added, “What could possibly go wrong now?”
Her question was rhetorical, and her deadpan expression made the class laugh.
They carried on without more trouble.

questions.question: What happened just before Maya and Leo began their presentation?
options: The screen went black and the slides disappeared.
The teacher asked them to leave the room.
The class had already seen the slides.
questions.answer: The screen went black and the slides disappeared.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says that the screen went black and the slides disappeared just before they began.

questions.question: Why did Maya stress the word “brilliant”?
options: She genuinely thought the equipment problem was helpful.
She used irony because the presentation had started badly.
She wanted Leo to speak more loudly.
questions.answer: She used irony because the presentation had started badly.
questions.explanation: A black screen and missing slides are not a brilliant start. The contrast shows that Maya meant the opposite.

questions.question: What does Leo's smile suggest?
options: He understood that Maya was being ironic.
He had not noticed the screen was black.
He was asking the teacher to cancel the presentation.
questions.answer: He understood that Maya was being ironic.
questions.explanation: The passage says Maya knew Leo understood the irony because he smiled.

questions.question: What was wrong when the slides returned?
options: The first slide was upside down.
The computer had no sound.
The slides belonged to another class.
questions.answer: The first slide was upside down.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says the slides returned, but the first one was upside down.

questions.question: Why does Leo say the technology is having “a bit of a difficult day”?
options: He uses understatement to describe the problems in a light way.
He thinks the computer is choosing to cause trouble.
He is giving the class a technical explanation.
questions.answer: He uses understatement to describe the problems in a light way.
questions.explanation: The phrase “a bit of a difficult day” softens the description of the screen and slide problems.

questions.question: What does Maya mean by “What could possibly go wrong now?”
options: She is making a rhetorical, ironic comment after the earlier problems.
She is asking the teacher to list possible technical problems.
She believes nothing else can go wrong.
questions.answer: She is making a rhetorical, ironic comment after the earlier problems.
questions.explanation: The question follows several problems, and the passage says it was rhetorical.

questions.question: What makes Maya's rhetorical question funny to the class?
options: Her deadpan expression.
Her use of a very high voice.
The teacher's explanation of the computer.
questions.explanation: The passage directly connects her deadpan expression with the class laughing.

questions.question: How did the presentation continue after the slides came back?
options: They carried on and had no more trouble.
They stopped and tried again the next day.
They asked the class to finish the project.
questions.answer: They carried on and had no more trouble.
questions.explanation: The passage says they carried on without more trouble.

questions.question: What does “not exactly as planned” imply about the start of the presentation?
options: It was stressful and went wrong in several ways.
It was exactly what Maya and Leo had expected.
The presentation was cancelled before it began.
questions.answer: It was stressful and went wrong in several ways.
questions.explanation: This understatement refers to the black screen, missing slides, and upside-down slide.

questions.question: Which clue helps readers recognise that Maya's “brilliant start” comment is ironic?
options: The equipment failed just before the presentation.
Maya and Leo were presenting a science project.
Their teacher was in the classroom.
questions.answer: The equipment failed just before the presentation.
questions.explanation: The failed equipment conflicts with the positive word “brilliant,” showing that Maya's comment is ironic.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Decoding Irony and Understatement in the Break Room

content.summary: Native speakers frequently use irony, deadpan tones, and litotes to handle awkward workplace failures. In this audio, two colleagues discuss a presentation that went wrong. You need to focus on intonation cues, dry pitch drops, and the contrast between literal words and real sentiment.
learningObjectives: Catch the real meaning behind polite litotes and dry understatements in conversation.
Identify cues that signal sarcasm, such as flat intonation and exaggerated word choice.
Notice consonant-to-vowel linking and intrusive glides in natural speech.

keyPhrases.note: A classic English understatement used to soften the mention of a total disaster.
Ironic praise directed at an event or mistake that made a bad situation worse.
Hyperbole paired with a flat or dropping tone to show obvious dissatisfaction.
Deliberately vague understatement to avoid stating bluntly how chaotic something was.

connectedSpeech.note: The negative contraction fuses with the vowel sound of our.
Smooth catenation links final consonants /v/, /p/, and /n/ across vowel boundaries.
The weak indefinite article links right into the initial vowel of inspired.
An intrusive /j/ glide joins the two vowel sounds across the word boundary.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Mastering Written Irony, Understatement, and Dry Wit

content.summary: This guide focuses on constructing subtle nuance in written English. You will learn to compose understated observations (litotes), friendly verbal irony, and dry commentary without relying on heavy punctuation or blunt criticism.

blueprintItems.title: The Litotes Formula for Polite Understatement
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + Negative Auxiliary + [exactly / entirely / particularly] + Positive Adjective / Noun Phrase
blueprintItems.example: His explanation was not exactly a model of clarity.

blueprintItems.title: The Ironic Contrast Construction
blueprintItems.formula: Superlative / Cheerful Adjective + Noun + Relative Clause exposing a bleak reality
blueprintItems.example: Brilliant work: another twenty-page report that nobody will ever open.

blueprintItems.title: The Rhetorical Dismissal Pattern
blueprintItems.formula: What / How + Auxiliary + Subject + [expect / suppose] + Clause?
blueprintItems.example: What did you expect would happen when you left the office windows open in a storm?

mechanicsRules.rule: Avoid using quotation marks to signal sarcasm. Let word choice establish the irony instead of relying on 'scare quotes'.
mechanicsRules.badExample: We had a "wonderful" time waiting three hours for our luggage.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: We had a wonderful time waiting three hours for our luggage.
mechanicsRules.why: Quotation marks make irony clumsy and obvious. Native B2 and C1 writing relies on context and tone to convey meaning.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a colon or a comma rather than an exclamation mark when delivering a dry, deadpan statement.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Oh great! Our flight got delayed again!
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Oh great, our flight got delayed again.
mechanicsRules.why: Exclamation points indicate genuine excitement or overt anger. A period or comma preserves the flat, understated tone characteristic of British and dry American irony.

mechanicsRules.rule: Place concessive adverbs like 'hardly' or 'scarcely' immediately before the main verb or adjective without splitting fixed idioms.
mechanicsRules.badExample: It was what I hardly would describe as a relaxing weekend.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: It was hardly what I would describe as a relaxing weekend.
mechanicsRules.why: Adverbs of degree must modify the entire predicate phrase correctly to sound natural.

sampleSentences.en: The final audit was slightly less comfortable than we had anticipated.
sampleSentences.id: Audit akhir tersebut sedikit kurang menyenangkan dari yang kami antisipasi.
sampleSentences.focus: Litotes through comparative softening ('slightly less comfortable')

sampleSentences.en: Splendid news: the server crashed five minutes before the submission deadline.
sampleSentences.id: Kabar luar biasa: server mogok lima menit sebelum batas akhir pengumpulan.
sampleSentences.focus: Ironic opening word paired with a factual catastrophe

sampleSentences.en: She was not overly pleased with having to redo the entire project over the weekend.
sampleSentences.id: Dia tidak terlalu senang karena harus mengerjakan ulang seluruh proyek di akhir pekan.

sampleSentences.en: How was I supposed to know the printer would catch fire after printing three pages?
sampleSentences.id: Bagaimana saya bisa tahu printer itu akan terbakar setelah mencetak tiga halaman?
sampleSentences.focus: Sarcastic rhetorical framing to displace blame

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: well that was "fantastic" news to receive on a monday morning
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Well, that was fantastic news to receive on a Monday morning.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Nah, itu kabar yang luar biasa untuk diterima pada Senin pagi.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Capitalize the first word and days of the week, insert an introductory comma, and remove ironic scare quotes.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: the hotel room wasnt exactly what we had booked in paris
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: The hotel room wasn't exactly what we had booked in Paris.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Kamar hotel itu tidak sepenuhnya seperti yang kami pesan di Paris.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Capitalize proper nouns and sentence starters, and add the missing apostrophe in negative contractions.

mechanicsChallenges.translation: Bagus sekali, kita harus berjalan lima mil lagi di bawah hujan.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Separate ironic initial exclamations with a comma and end with a full stop instead of multiple exclamation marks.

guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three to four sentences reviewing a disappointing dining experience using litotes and understatement. Use phrases like 'not exactly', 'rather less than', or 'hardly' instead of angry complaints.
guidedLabChallenges.example: The soup was not exactly boiling when it arrived at our table. Our waiter was rather less attentive than one might have hoped on a quiet Tuesday evening. It was hardly a memorable gastronomic occasion.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the blunt criticism using litotes with 'not exactly':
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'was not exactly' followed by a positive noun phrase like 'a success' or 'a masterpiece'.
targetAnswers: The presentation was not exactly a success.
The presentation was not exactly a triumph.
The presentation was not exactly a masterpiece.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Litotes replaces direct negative adjectives like 'terrible' with a negated positive word to create polite understatement.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence into dry irony starting with 'Just what I needed':
practicumQuestions.promptText: I really did not want another task on my desk today.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use a positive sarcastic frame: 'Just what I needed today, another task on my desk.'
targetAnswers: Just what I needed, another task on my desk.
Just what I needed today: another task on my desk.
Just what I needed, another task on my desk today.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Ironic statements often express the precise opposite of the speaker's true feeling to produce dry humor.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two clauses into one sentence using 'although' to create an understated contrast:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Clause A: The hotel room was tiny. Clause B: The brochure had promised a spacious suite.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'Although the brochure had promised a spacious suite, ...'
targetAnswers: Although the brochure had promised a spacious suite, the hotel room was tiny.
The hotel room was tiny, although the brochure had promised a spacious suite.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concession that highlights the gap between expectation and reality.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the punctuation and quotation marks to create a natural, deadpan sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: oh wonderful! we have got a flat tyre in the middle of "nowhere"!
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first word, replace excessive exclamation points with a comma and full stop, and remove the quotation marks.
targetAnswers: Oh wonderful, we have got a flat tyre in the middle of nowhere.
Oh wonderful, we have got a flat tire in the middle of nowhere.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Dry sarcasm works best without exclamation marks and without scare quotes around ordinary nouns.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform the direct question into a sarcastic rhetorical question starting with 'What did you expect':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Why are you surprised that the dog ate the steak you left on the floor?
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'What did you expect would happen when ...'
targetAnswers: What did you expect would happen when you left the steak on the floor?
What did you expect when you left the steak on the floor?
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'What did you expect would happen...' signals that the negative outcome was completely predictable.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Join the clauses using 'hardly' to form an understated observation:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Clause 1: The lecture was boring. Clause 2: It did not inspire any of the students.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the structure: 'The lecture was hardly inspiring for the students.' or 'The lecture was boring and hardly inspired any of the students.'
targetAnswers: The lecture was hardly inspiring for any of the students.
The lecture was boring, and it hardly inspired any of the students.
The lecture was hardly what I would call inspiring.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Hardly' softens the criticism into an understated, sophisticated B2 observation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the capitalization, comma splice, and punctuation in this sarcastic comment:
practicumQuestions.promptText: brilliant news the budget cuts affect our project first
practicumQuestions.hint: Add a colon or comma after 'Brilliant news' and finish with a period.
targetAnswers: Brilliant news: the budget cuts affect our project first.
Brilliant news, the budget cuts affect our project first.
practicumQuestions.explanation: An introductory ironic announcement requires proper capitalization and punctuation to introduce the following clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to the situation using the litotes phrase 'not exactly thrilled':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Situation: Your manager tells you that you must work late on Friday evening.
practicumQuestions.hint: Write a complete sentence such as 'I am not exactly thrilled about working late on Friday.'
targetAnswers: I am not exactly thrilled about working late on Friday.
I was not exactly thrilled about having to work late on Friday.
I am not exactly thrilled to work late on Friday evening.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Not exactly thrilled' is a common B2 litotes formula used to voice dissatisfaction politely.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the statement to make it an understatement using 'a bit of an understatement':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Calling that disastrous storm a light shower is completely ridiculous.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'To call that storm a light shower is ...'
targetAnswers: To call that storm a light shower is a bit of an understatement.
Calling that storm a light shower is a bit of an understatement.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Using 'a bit of an understatement' directly names the rhetorical device to highlight an absurd minimization.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write an ironic one-sentence remark about pouring rain on a beach holiday, beginning with 'Perfect weather':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Situation: It has rained all day on your summer beach holiday.
practicumQuestions.hint: Write: 'Perfect weather for a swim in the sea.' or 'Perfect weather for building sandcastles.'
targetAnswers: Perfect weather for a day at the beach.
Perfect weather for a swim in the sea.
Perfect weather for sunbathing outside.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Labeling terrible weather as 'perfect' for an outdoor activity is an iconic form of friendly irony.

content.summary: Use understatement to describe something as less serious or impressive than it really is. Friendly irony can gently point out a contrast between what someone says and what is happening. Sarcasm is sharper and may sound critical, so consider your relationship with the listener. A deadpan delivery keeps your face and voice calm, while tongue-in-cheek comments are clearly playful in context.
content.audioGuidance: Listen for context as well as words. Speakers may lower their pitch at the end of a dry or ironic comment, or use a small pitch change to make the joke clear. Keep the delivery controlled rather than exaggerated. Pause briefly before the ironic detail, stress the key contrast, and use a warm expression when you want the comment to sound friendly. If the listener might mistake sarcasm for a serious criticism, choose a more direct and kind phrasing.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Keep stressed vowels clear in words such as ironic, sarcasm, and understatement.
pillars.explanation: Give the main vowel in each stressed syllable enough time to be heard. Do not rush the longer word understatement; divide it into syllables before saying it at a natural pace.

pillars.name: Syllable Stress
pillars.target: Place stress correctly in multi-syllable vocabulary.
pillars.explanation: Say UNDERstatement, SARCasm, DEADpan, and iRONic with the main stress on the capitalised syllable. Correct stress makes these words easier to recognise.

pillars.name: Pitch and Intonation
pillars.target: Use pitch changes to signal contrast without overacting.
pillars.explanation: A lower ending pitch can make a comment sound dry or deadpan. A slight rise on a key word can signal playful disbelief, but context and facial expression should support the meaning.

pillars.name: Tone and Audience
pillars.target: Make friendly irony distinct from hurtful sarcasm.
pillars.explanation: Use a relaxed pace and a warm tone with friends. Avoid a sharp or contemptuous voice when you are joking, especially with people who may not know your sense of humour.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Both words carry their main stress on the first syllable. Keep the remaining syllables lighter.
Give deadpan one strong first beat. In tongue-in-cheek, the main stress falls on tongue and cheek.
Notice the stress change: ironic is stressed on the second syllable, while irony is stressed on the first.
Pitch has one syllable. In sarcastic, place the main stress on the second syllable.

drills.targetText: Calling that long wait a little delay is an understatement.
drills.phonetic: /ˈkɔːlɪŋ ðæt lɒŋ weɪt ə ˈlɪtl dɪˈleɪ ɪz ən ˈʌndəˌsteɪtmənt/
drills.focus: Clear stress in understatement and natural linking
drills.hint: Stress UNDER in understatement, then say the whole sentence smoothly without giving every word equal weight.

drills.targetText: Well, that was a brilliant time to forget the tickets.
drills.phonetic: /wel ðæt wəz ə ˈbrɪliənt taɪm tə fəˈɡet ðə ˈtɪkɪts/
drills.hint: Stress brilliant lightly to show the contrast, then keep your voice friendly so the comment sounds playful.

drills.targetText: It is a bit chilly in this room.
drills.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ə bɪt ˈtʃɪli ɪn ðɪs ruːm/
drills.focus: Understatement with a controlled, calm delivery
drills.hint: Say the sentence calmly even if the room is very cold. Let the situation make the understatement clear.

drills.targetText: Oh, great, the printer has stopped working again.
drills.phonetic: /əʊ ɡreɪt ðə ˈprɪntə hæz stɒpt ˈwɜːkɪŋ əˈɡen/
drills.hint: Use a small rise on great, then lower your pitch at the end. Keep the tone dry rather than angry.

roleplay.context: You and a colleague are preparing for a presentation when the office printer breaks for the third time. Practise a friendly ironic response, then make sure your colleague understands that you are joking.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: The printer has stopped working again, just as we need the handouts.
turns.translation: Printernya berhenti bekerja lagi, tepat saat kita membutuhkan bahan cetaknya.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Oh, perfect timing. Our office equipment really knows how to help.
turns.translation: Wah, waktunya benar-benar pas. Peralatan kantor kita memang tahu cara membantu.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Are you being serious, or are you joking?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I am joking, of course. It is a bit of a problem, but we can share the digital version.
turns.translation: Tentu saja saya bercanda. Ini memang sedikit masalah, tetapi kita bisa membagikan versi digitalnya.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds. Tell a short story about a plan that went wrong, and include one clear understatement.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe a time when something did not go as planned. What happened, and how did you describe it to someone?
storyPoints: Explain what you planned to do and what unexpected problem occurred.
Describe how you reacted or what you said at the time.
Include an understatement that makes the problem sound milder than it really was.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The train was two hours late, so calling it a small delay was an understatement.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə treɪn wəz tuː ˈaʊəz leɪt səʊ ˈkɔːlɪŋ ɪt ə smɔːl dɪˈleɪ wəz ən ˈʌndəˌsteɪtmənt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Give enough detail to make the situation clear, then use understatement naturally. Keep your tone calm rather than making the story sound like a complaint.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds. Tell a story about an inconvenient or funny situation and use one friendly ironic comment.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell a short story about a moment when something happened at exactly the wrong time. How did you react?
storyPoints: Set the scene and explain what you expected to happen.
Describe the event that created an unexpected contrast.
Add a tongue-in-cheek comment and explain how people reacted.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: It started raining just as we sat down for our picnic, which was excellent timing.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪt ˈstɑːtɪd ˈreɪnɪŋ dʒʌst əz wiː sæt daʊn fə ə ˈpɪknɪk wɪtʃ wəz ˈeksələnt ˈtaɪmɪŋ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Make the contrast between the situation and your comment easy to understand. Use a light tone so the irony sounds friendly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond in character for at least four turns. Use friendly irony, then make your meaning clear if asked.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Roleplay a conversation with a friend whose outdoor event has been interrupted by heavy rain.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Your friend has just arrived at an outdoor event in heavy rain. They are disappointed, but you want to make a gentle joke and help them feel better.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the friend's supportive companion. Make one light ironic comment about the weather, then offer a practical suggestion.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The weather has certainly chosen a perfect moment to be dramatic.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈweðə həz ˈsɜːtnli ˈtʃəʊzən ə ˈpɜːfɪkt ˈməʊmənt tə biː drəˈmætɪk/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Keep the joke gentle and respond to your friend's feelings. Show that you are being supportive, not mocking them.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond in character for at least four turns. Use a deadpan line, then clarify that you are joking if your listener is unsure.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Roleplay a conversation with a classmate after you both discover that the classroom is locked before an important presentation.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You and a classmate have arrived early to practise, but the classroom is locked and the presentation begins soon.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the classmate's partner. Deliver one short deadpan comment, listen to the response, and suggest a useful next step.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: A locked classroom is exactly what we needed this morning.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ə lɒkt ˈklɑːsruːm ɪz ɪɡˈzæktli wɒt wiː ˈniːdɪd ðɪs ˈmɔːnɪŋ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a calm, serious delivery for the deadpan comment. Make the joke clear through context and follow it with a helpful suggestion.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond in character for at least four turns. Explain why a sarcastic remark might be misunderstood and rephrase it more kindly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Roleplay a conversation with a colleague who has misunderstood your comment about a delayed report.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A colleague worked late to finish a report. You made a sarcastic comment about how quickly it arrived, and they took it as criticism.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the speaker who made the comment. Acknowledge the misunderstanding, apologise, and explain your real meaning without blaming your colleague.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I am sorry, that sounded more critical than I intended. I appreciate the work you put into it.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ əm ˈsɒri ðæt ˈsaʊndɪd mɔː ˈkrɪtɪkəl ðən aɪ ɪnˈtendɪd aɪ əˈpriːʃieɪt ðə wɜːk juː pʊt ˈɪntuː ɪt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Show awareness that sarcasm can sound hurtful. Use a sincere tone and choose clear, respectful language when repairing the misunderstanding.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond in character for at least four turns. Describe the irony in the situation and use an appropriate tone.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Roleplay a conversation with a friend about a café that has run out of coffee.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You and a friend visit a café famous for its coffee, but the café has run out of coffee on the day of a local coffee festival.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a friend chatting about the surprising situation. Point out the irony with a tongue-in-cheek comment, then keep the conversation warm.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: It is rather ironic that the coffee festival's best-known café has no coffee today.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈrɑːðər aɪˈrɒnɪk ðət ðə ˈkɒfi ˈfestɪvəlz best nəʊn ˈkæfeɪ hæz nəʊ ˈkɒfi təˈdeɪ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Explain the contrast between what people expect and what happened. Keep your voice amused rather than annoyed.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds. Explain the difference between understatement, friendly irony, and sarcasm, then give one short example of each.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: How is an understatement different from sarcasm? Include an example of a tongue-in-cheek comment.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Calling a very long wait a short delay is an understatement, while a sarcastic comment may sound more critical.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈkɔːlɪŋ ə ˈveri lɒŋ weɪt ə ʃɔːt dɪˈleɪ ɪz ən ˈʌndəˌsteɪtmənt waɪl ə sɑːˈkæstɪk ˈkɒment meɪ saʊnd mɔː ˈkrɪtɪkəl/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use the vocabulary accurately and make the difference in tone clear. Choose examples that show how the speaker's intention affects the listener.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence aloud in two different ways, using 'although' or 'even though' to show the contrast between the words and the situation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The room was extremely hot. Begin with: 'Even though it was extremely hot...' Finish by describing an understatement.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Even though it was extremely hot, I called it a little warm.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈiːvən ðəʊ ɪt wəz ɪkˈstriːmli hɒt aɪ kɔːld ɪt ə ˈlɪtl wɔːm/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use although or even though to connect the real situation with the milder description. Keep the contrast grammatically complete and easy to follow.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say each word clearly, then use it in a short sentence: understatement, sarcasm, deadpan, and ironic. Make the stressed syllable clear without exaggerating it.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Listen to your own recording and check the main stress in UNDERstatement, SARCasm, DEADpan, and iRONic.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: He gave a deadpan response to the ironic comment.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /hiː ɡeɪv ə ˈdedpæn rɪˈspɒns tə ði aɪˈrɒnɪk ˈkɒment/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Make the stressed syllable prominent while keeping the other syllables shorter and lighter. Check especially that the stress in ironic falls on the second syllable.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the ironic comment once with a small rise on the key word and a falling ending. Then say it again with a warm, ordinary tone to compare the effect.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Practise the line: 'Oh, brilliant, the bus has just left.' Use pitch carefully so it sounds ironic rather than genuinely pleased.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Oh, brilliant, the bus has just left.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /əʊ ˈbrɪliənt ðə bʌs həz dʒʌst left/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a slight rise on brilliant to signal contrast, then let your pitch fall at the end. Keep the delivery controlled, and avoid sounding angry or theatrical.
